emerald-cave.alt: Inside Emerald Cave on the Colorado River: dark volcanic walls lit from below by emerald-green water, with two kayakers at the cave mouth
emerald-cave.caption: The glow is light physics: midday sun through the south-facing mouth, clear water, algae on the riverbed reflecting green. It needs a clear sky, flat water and a high sun.

emerald-cave-tour-operators.alt: Kayaks lined up on the Willow Beach launch ramp with a guide briefing a group, Black Canyon upstream
emerald-cave-tour-operators.caption: Willow Beach: where every half-day tour and every rental launches. Two miles upstream is the cave.

emerald-cave-kayak-rental.alt: A lone paddler in a rented sit-on-top kayak heading upstream through Black Canyon on calm green water
emerald-cave-kayak-rental.caption: Self-guided: about 2.2 miles upstream from Willow Beach on flat, cold water, then the same way back. Be on the water by 9 am, before the afternoon wind.

hoover-dam-kayak-launch.alt: Kayaks on the water directly below Hoover Dam with the dam and the bypass bridge towering above
hoover-dam-kayak-launch.caption: The only way onto this water: an NPS-authorized outfitter in the restricted launch window. Twelve miles downstream to Willow Beach.

is-emerald-cave-worth-it.alt: Four kayaks queuing outside the glowing mouth of Emerald Cave at midday in Black Canyon
is-emerald-cave-worth-it.caption: The cave fits three to six kayaks. Midday on a summer weekend means a queue; the 3 to 4 pm sparkle window is usually empty.

las-vegas-colorado-river-tours.alt: A raft and kayaks drifting down the calm Colorado River through Black Canyon, with a steaming hot-spring side canyon
las-vegas-colorado-river-tours.caption: Kayak, raft or float: one calm stretch of river, Class I flatwater, no rapids, cold and clear all year.

las-vegas-stargazing-tour.alt: The Milky Way over the red sandstone of Red Rock Canyon with the faint glow of Las Vegas on the horizon and two people at a telescope
las-vegas-stargazing-tour.caption: Stargazing in Vegas means leaving Vegas: the Strip is a Bortle 9 sky, Red Rock is thirty minutes away. Plan by the moon, not the calendar.

natural-attractions-near-las-vegas.alt: The red and cream sandstone of the Calico Hills at Red Rock Canyon with the scenic loop road and two hikers
natural-attractions-near-las-vegas.caption: Red Rock Canyon, seventeen miles from the Strip: the closest escape and the first rung on the ladder of day trips.

tours-from-las-vegas-to-antelope-canyon.alt: The swirling sandstone walls of Lower Antelope Canyon with a steel staircase and two visitors with a guide
tours-from-las-vegas-to-antelope-canyon.caption: Lower Antelope: ladders and stairs, fewer people, no light beams. Upper is the flat walk-in with the midday beams. Navajo-guided only, either way.

vegas-night-helicopter-tour.alt: A sightseeing helicopter over the Las Vegas Strip at night with the lit resort corridor below
vegas-night-helicopter-tour.caption: Ten to fifteen minutes in the air: up the Strip, on to downtown and the STRAT, and back. Strip only, no canyon after dark.

hoover-dam-tours-from-las-vegas.alt: Hoover Dam from the memorial bridge walkway, with the intake towers and the road across the crest
hoover-dam-tours-from-las-vegas.caption: The best view is free: the bridge walkway. Dam tickets are separate from any Vegas tour fare.

emerald-cave-glow-windows.alt: Timeline of when Emerald Cave glows: the 10 am to 2 pm primary window with an 11 to 1 peak, the 3 to 4 pm sparkle window, and the winter shift to 10 to 11 am
emerald-cave-glow-windows.caption: Two windows, one cave. The midday glow is the famous one; the afternoon sparkle is the quiet one.

emerald-cave-season-guide.alt: Season guide for Emerald Cave: October to April recommended, March to May windy, June to August hot with queues, September to November shoulder season
emerald-cave-season-guide.caption: The cave fits three to six kayaks at a time, which is why the calendar matters as much as the clock.

rent-vs-guided-emerald-cave.alt: Comparison of renting a kayak for Emerald Cave versus taking a guided tour: price, pace, guidance, logistics and who each suits
rent-vs-guided-emerald-cave.caption: Same launch, same route, same cave. The difference is freedom and price against a leader and zero planning.

hoover-dam-kayak-launch-rules.alt: The rules for kayaking from Hoover Dam: no self-launch at the security zone, NPS-authorized outfitters only, the $30 to $32 permit, the $25 vehicle fee, and the 12-mile route
hoover-dam-kayak-launch-rules.caption: No walk-up launch exists at the dam. The permit is per person and mandatory; ask whether it is in the price.

black-canyon-hazards.alt: The three hazards on the Colorado River at Black Canyon: afternoon wind, 54 degree water, and drowning without a life jacket
black-canyon-hazards.caption: Guides, rangers and rescue teams report the same three. All three are handled by launching early and keeping the jacket on.

emerald-cave-worth-it-verdict.alt: Three ways an Emerald Cave visit can go: the midday glow with its queue, the quiet 3 to 4 pm sparkle, and the wrong window with no glow
emerald-cave-worth-it-verdict.caption: The disappointed reviews are almost all the third panel. Pick the window, then the tour.

colorado-river-tours-modes.alt: Comparison of the three ways to travel the Colorado River below Hoover Dam: kayak, motor-assisted raft and float, all on Class I flatwater
colorado-river-tours-modes.caption: One stretch of water, three ways to travel it. None of them involve rapids.

natural-attractions-near-las-vegas-dista.alt: Distance ladder of natural attractions from the Las Vegas Strip, from Red Rock Canyon at 30 minutes to Antelope Canyon at 4.5 hours
natural-attractions-near-las-vegas-dista.caption: Plan by the hours you have. Everything above Valley of Fire is a full day.

upper-vs-lower-antelope-canyon.alt: Comparison of Upper and Lower Antelope Canyon: terrain, light beams, crowds, price and access, both Navajo-guided only
upper-vs-lower-antelope-canyon.caption: Most Vegas tours make you pick one. The beams are Upper's; the quiet is Lower's.

hoover-dam-tours-half-day-vs-combo.alt: Hoover Dam tours from Las Vegas compared: the half-day dam tour versus the Grand Canyon West combo, and the three separate dam tickets
hoover-dam-tours-half-day-vs-combo.caption: Your tour fare and your dam ticket are different purchases. The deep Guided Dam Tour is self-drive-only in practice.

las-vegas-stargazing-timing.alt: Stargazing timing near Las Vegas: plan around the new moon, Milky Way core June to August, winter for Orion, and the drive to Red Rock or Death Valley
las-vegas-stargazing-timing.caption: The moon is the biggest lever. After that, the season decides what you see, and the drive decides how dark it gets.
